# Backup & restore

Export everything zt currently manages to a portable manifest:

```bash
zt export                   # writes zt.yaml in the current directory
zt export -o ~/backup/zt.yaml
```

The generated `zt.yaml` captures the intent behind each tunnel — port,
protocol, access policy — but deliberately excludes credentials and
Cloudflare-specific IDs. It is safe to commit to git.

```yaml
# zt.yaml — portable cfzt service manifest
# generated by `zt export` — credentials are NOT included here.
# on a new machine: run `zt init` first, then `zt apply zt.yaml`

services:
  grafana:
    port: 3000
  portainer:
    docker: true
    allow:
      - you@example.com
  multi:
    docker: true
    container_port: '443'   # pick a specific published port when the
                             # container publishes more than one
  vault:
    port: 8200
    protocol: quic
  api:
    port: 8080
    public: true
```

To recreate the same setup on a different machine:

```bash
# 1. on the new machine — configure credentials
zt init

# 2. apply the manifest
zt apply zt.yaml
```

`zt apply` diffs the manifest against the local state and only creates what
is missing. Existing tunnels are never modified or deleted automatically —
a service already present in local state is reported and skipped, so
running `zt apply` twice with the same manifest on the same machine is
safe and doesn't create duplicate tunnels:

```
⚡ Applying zt.yaml

  plan: to create: 3   skipped: 1   untracked: 0

  ~ api                 already exists — skipping

  ⚡ Bringing up grafana.example.com → localhost:3000
  ...
  🎉 Ready: https://grafana.example.com

  ✅ Done — 3 service(s) created
```

If a service exists locally but is absent from the manifest, `zt apply`
reports it without touching it — remove it explicitly with `zt down <name>`
if needed.
